question: Under exactly which feature-dimension, regularization, bias, and balance regimes does regularized MSE have neural-collapse global minimizers or a strict-saddle landscape in the unconstrained-feature model, and do the paper's rescaled-loss geometry, end-to-end experiments, and released artifact justify its broader claims about optimization, architecture independence, and efficiency?

key_findings.claim: The paper gives a useful closed-form characterization of the regularized vanilla-MSE global minimizers under balanced unconstrained features.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 3.1 reduces the solution to singular-value thresholding and separates the regimes by lambda_W lambda_H, feature dimension d, and bias penalty lambda_b. The appendix derives the optimum by first solving the regularized matrix-factorization problem for fixed bias and then optimizing the singular values induced by the bias.

anchors.section: Appendix B, Theorem B.1 and Equation 10

key_findings.claim: When lambda_W lambda_H is below 1/(NK), every characterized global minimizer has within-class collapse and scaled self-duality.
key_findings.evidence: The theorem sets every feature h_{k,i} equal to its class mean and relates that mean to the matching classifier row by h_k=sqrt(lambda_W/(lambda_H n)) w_k. This establishes NC1 and NC3 inside the theorem's balanced free-feature model.

anchors.section: Theorem B.1, NC1 and NC3 clause

key_findings.claim: The abstract's emphatic statement that the only global minimizers are neural-collapse solutions is false under the theorem's own regularization regimes.
key_findings.evidence: The abstract says the '(only!) global minimizers are neural collapse solutions,' but Theorem 3.1 explicitly gives W*=0 and H*=0 whenever lambda_W lambda_H is at least 1/(NK). That zero solution has neither a nondegenerate simplex ETF nor meaningful self-dual class geometry.

key_findings.claim: The conclusion's statement that all global solutions exhibit neural collapse also conflicts with the d<K-1 regime.
key_findings.evidence: For d<K-1, the theorem yields only a best rank-d approximation of the centered simplex Gram matrix. The authors themselves state that the resulting class means have neither equal length nor maximal pairwise distance, so canonical NC2 does not hold even in the nonzero regime.

key_findings.claim: The low-dimensional global geometry is nonunique, a point hidden by the notation P_d.
key_findings.evidence: The centered K-class simplex projector has K-1 identical nonzero singular values. For d<K-1, any d-dimensional subspace of that eigenspace is an equally good rank-d approximation, so the theorem permits a continuum of class configurations rather than selecting one reproducible geometry.

key_findings.claim: The bias term materially changes whether the nonzero high-dimensional MSE optimum is a simplex ETF.
key_findings.evidence: For d at least K, Theorem 3.1 has two lambda_b regimes; the centered simplex form appears only under the stated bias-penalty condition. The discussion notes that as lambda_b tends to infinity, the no-bias optimum becomes orthonormal rather than a simplex ETF.

anchors.section: Appendix B.4, d=K and d>K cases

key_findings.claim: The global-optimality theory does not cover the rescaled MSE objective used for miniImageNet.
key_findings.evidence: Section 3.1 explicitly says its analysis is only for vanilla MSE and leaves joint alpha,M analysis to future work. Therefore Figure 6 cannot be described as verification of the theorem for the rescaled loss; it is an empirical extrapolation to a different objective.

key_findings.claim: The no-bias regularized matrix-factorization subproblem has a plausible all-d strict-saddle characterization.
key_findings.evidence: Lemma B.2 balances the factors, aligns nonzero factor directions with singular vectors of the target, identifies soft-thresholded global products, and constructs a negative-curvature direction whenever a qualifying singular component is missing. This is the paper's most self-contained landscape result.

key_findings.claim: The full biased strict-saddle theorem is restricted to d>K and is not proved in the paper.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 3.3 assumes d>K. Its explanation says the result follows because a technique from the authors' earlier CE paper holds for any smooth convex loss, and gives no detailed bias-inclusive proof here. The cases d<=K are explicitly left open.

anchors.section: Discussion and proof sketch after Theorem 3.3

key_findings.claim: The claim that any saddle-escaping method converges to an NC global solution is broader than the cited landscape result.
key_findings.evidence: Strict-saddle geometry alone does not guarantee convergence of arbitrary stochastic or deterministic algorithms. Almost-sure results require specified algorithms, initialization, step-size/noise, smoothness, boundedness, and convergence assumptions; even then the attained global solution can be zero or non-simplex in theorem-covered regimes.

key_findings.claim: None of the strict-saddle results transfers directly from free H to end-to-end ResNet optimization.
key_findings.evidence: The theory optimizes one independent feature vector per training sample with a direct Frobenius penalty on H. Practical training ties every feature through shared nonlinear network parameters and penalizes parameters rather than H; the paper offers only an upper-bound analogy and earlier empirical precedent for this substitution.

anchors.section: Discussion of feature versus parameter weight decay
Consequence conditional on H being free

key_findings.claim: The appendix's matrix-product notation is dimensionally inconsistent in several proof lines.
key_findings.evidence: With W in R^{Kxd} and H in R^{dxN}, the valid prediction product is WH. Pages 23-24 repeatedly print WH^T or sums of w_i h_i^T while simultaneously treating the result as KxN; the intended algebra is recoverable, but the displayed dimensions are wrong.

anchors.section: Appendix B.2, product expansion after Equation 22
Appendix B.2, Cases I-II and Equation 23

key_findings.claim: Equation 24 has a factor-of-two labeling inconsistency in the directional Hessian.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix defines the Hessian bilinear form conventionally, but labels the displayed quadratic expression as 2[∇²xi](Delta,Delta). Direct differentiation of one-half times the squared residual plus one-half regularizers gives the displayed right-hand side as the second directional derivative itself. The sign argument survives, but the equality as printed is inconsistent.

key_findings.claim: The rescaled-MSE derivation contains a substantive target inconsistency between Equations 4, 30, and 31.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 4 uses the one-hot target MY, so incorrect-class targets are zero. Equation 30 instead squares each incorrect logit minus one, while Equation 31 drops that minus one and the released loss code also uses zero incorrect targets. Exact arXiv source and the official PMLR camera PDF preserve this mismatch, showing Equation 30 is not a text-extraction artifact.

key_findings.claim: The landscape visualization is a highly constrained slice, not evidence about the full practical optimization landscape or convergence rate.
key_findings.evidence: It fixes b=0 and W at a global simplex ETF, varies one feature only in the span of two classifier vectors, and later takes K to infinity. It therefore removes the coupled W,H,b dynamics and network parameterization whose optimization behavior is at issue; the conclusion itself calls these simplifications extravagant.

key_findings.claim: The released landscape artifact is not a complete, parameterized reproduction script.
key_findings.evidence: At official HEAD 47624073359bbaa691b4ddc0057dd118e14e70a0, figs/visualization/MSE_landscape_python.txt hard-codes K=500 and the vanilla expression; alternatives are manually commented expressions. There is no command, environment, test, or exact figure provenance tying it to every panel.

key_findings.claim: Figure 3 does not show all NC metrics converging to zero regardless of optimizer, contrary to the prose.
key_findings.evidence: The plotted NC2 curves visibly plateau above zero by epoch 200, around 0.04 for SGD and roughly 0.13-0.15 for Adam and L-BFGS. The categorical sentence that NC1, NC2, and NC3 converge to zero is therefore not supported even by the displayed single runs.

key_findings.claim: The three-optimizer comparison does not isolate optimizer choice and its L-BFGS settings disagree across paper and artifact.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix specifies L-BFGS learning rate 0.01, while official cmds_mse.sh and README use 0.1. The commands use batch 512 for L-BFGS and different defaults for SGD/Adam; README gives yet another batch 2048. The implementation applies L-BFGS with line search to stochastic mini-batches, not a matched full-batch method.

key_findings.claim: Every empirical curve is effectively a single-run descriptive result.
key_findings.evidence: No figure reports repeated seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, statistical tests, or raw numerical tables. The repository sets one default seed and publishes no result files or checkpoints, so small optimizer, dimension, alpha, and M differences cannot be separated from run variance.

key_findings.claim: The feature-dimension sweep changes the network architecture and capacity, not only the last feature dimension d.
key_findings.evidence: In official models/resnet.py lines 194-203, the fixdim option changes the output channels of the final residual block. Thus Figure 4 jointly changes representation dimension, layer width, parameter count, and backbone capacity; it is not a controlled test of the theorem's free-feature dimensional threshold.

anchors.section: Figure 4 and choice of feature dimension

key_findings.claim: The fixed-ETF experiment supports comparable accuracy in one run, but not the README's claimed memory mechanism.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 5 visually reports similar learned-versus-fixed trajectories. Static parameter counting at official HEAD gives 11,173,962 trainable parameters for the standard d=512 learned model and 11,168,842 for fixed ETF, only about 0.046% less. Shrinking the final block to d=10 yields about 20.7% fewer parameters, so nearly all of the README's '>20% memory reduction' comes from narrowing the backbone, not fixing the classifier; no runtime-memory benchmark is supplied.

anchors.section: Improving efficiency via fixed simplex ETFs

key_findings.claim: The implemented numerical-rank metric is the square root of the metric stated in the paper.
key_findings.evidence: The paper defines the matrix analogue of numerical sparsity as the squared nuclear norm divided by squared Frobenius norm. Official validate_NC.py lines 166-176 returns nuclear norm divided by Frobenius norm without squaring either quantity, so a plotted value would not implement the stated definition.

key_findings.claim: The released code cannot reproduce Figure 6's numerical-rank panels at any official main-branch revision.
key_findings.evidence: Official validate_NC.py computes the nuclear metric near line 286 but line 307 comments out the append into info['nuclear_metric']. Consequently the saved list is empty and downstream plot scripts have no rank trajectory. This comment is present from the first substantive July 2022 artifact upload through HEAD.

key_findings.claim: The released cosine-margin computation does not implement the centered numerator defined in the paper.
key_findings.evidence: The paper defines cos(theta_{k,i;j}) using <w_j-w_G,h_{k,i}-h_G>. In validate_NC.py lines 179-209, the denominator centers W but the numerator is the model output minus b, equal to w_j^T h; it never subtracts w_G or h_G cross terms. The reported P_CM therefore equals the stated measure only under additional exact-centering conditions.

key_findings.claim: The NC validation pipeline uses fresh stochastic training augmentations rather than fixed training features.
key_findings.evidence: With the repository's --SOTA path, validate_NC.py iterates the training DataLoader containing random crop and flip transforms for every checkpoint. The plotted H metrics therefore vary with newly augmented views as well as with learned parameters, while the theorem assumes a fixed matrix of per-sample free features.

key_findings.claim: The released miniImageNet training route contradicts the appendix scheduler and crashes if the named scheduler is selected.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix A specifies CosineAnnealingWarmRestarts with T0=200 and eta_min=1e-4. Official commands omit --decay_type, so the default StepLR is used instead. In utils.py lines 69-76, choosing cos_anneal_warmup assigns misspelled variable schduler and then returns undefined scheduler, raising an error.

key_findings.claim: The seed configuration is internally inconsistent and supplies no multi-seed evidence.
key_findings.evidence: The artifact's set_seed requests deterministic cuDNN and benchmark=False, but argument processing later enables cuDNN benchmark by default. Only seed 6 is exposed in the supplied commands; there are no repetitions or seed-indexed raw results.

key_findings.claim: The miniImageNet dataset artifact is not self-contained or robustly versioned.
key_findings.evidence: The loader depends on an external Kaggle pickle with no checksum or version. It ignores the supplied class-dictionary values and assumes images are stored in contiguous class blocks, making the paper's 50,000/10,000 split sensitive to an undocumented serialization layout.

key_findings.claim: The README's advertised reproduction commands do not match the current parser or model inventory.
key_findings.evidence: The README names unsupported datasets MNIST and cifar10_random, absent models MLP and ResNet18_adapt, and invalid flags such as --ETF, --sep_decay, --width, and --depth; the actual fixed-classifier flag is --ETF_fc. A clean user cannot reproduce the advertised commands from official HEAD.

key_findings.claim: Several artifact defects independently prevent clean figure reproduction.
key_findings.evidence: The ETF helper hard-codes CUDA, split_array uses the requested batch size rather than number of splits in an exactly divisible branch, and plotting joins a repository path with an absolute '/imgs/...' suffix that discards the repository prefix and normally writes to a protected root directory. No tests exercise these routes.

key_findings.claim: The official artifact does not establish exact result provenance.
key_findings.evidence: The repository has 23 commits but no tags, releases, CI, tests, lock file, requirements file, license, checkpoints, raw info.pkl outputs, or numerical result tables. The first substantive camera-ready code/results-plot upload is dated 2022-07-19, four months after arXiv v2 and during ICML, and no commit is identified as the executed paper state.

key_findings.claim: Figure 6 supports at most a single-run association, not the claimed general law that larger alpha or M improves NC and performance.
key_findings.evidence: The twelve panels show selected trajectories for one miniImageNet setup, but no repeats, uncertainty, matched scheduler provenance, or full numeric values. Alpha and M also change target scale and gradient magnitude, so a positive visual association cannot isolate the proposed angular-conditioning mechanism.

key_findings.claim: Figure 7 cannot support the broad statement that CE features are more diverse and discriminative.
key_findings.evidence: It shows 100 selected training points per class from one d=3 run, with no seed, sample-selection rule, quantitative separation metric, test behavior, or uncertainty. The plot is illustrative and the two losses may also differ in optimization status.

key_findings.claim: The paper's balanced-class assumption is central and limits the scope of its global geometry.
key_findings.evidence: Every theorem uses K classes with exactly n samples each and a uniform one-hot label matrix. Imbalance can alter class norms, angles, bias, and even cause minority collapse, so the results cannot be read as a general characterization of classification training.

key_findings.claim: The paper proves no generalization theorem and NC metrics are not sufficient evidence of test performance.
key_findings.evidence: The theory concerns regularized training loss and free training features only. Figure 3 itself shows similar collapse tendencies alongside different test accuracies, and later work explicitly studies limitations of NC for generalization. The paper's test-performance explanations are correlations, not consequences of its theorems.

key_findings.claim: The defensible novelty is narrower than the paper's broad neural-collapse framing.
key_findings.evidence: Neural collapse, unconstrained features, MSE collapse/dynamics, and a concurrent MSE global-minimizer result all predate or coincide with this work. The main incremental contribution is a detailed regularized vanilla-MSE solution across bias and dimension regimes plus an all-d strict-saddle analysis for the fixed-bias/no-bias matrix factorization; the full biased strict-saddle template is imported from the same group's CE work.

method.core_idea: Replace the penultimate-layer outputs of a balanced K-class training set by free variables H, optimize a separately regularized affine classifier under vanilla MSE, characterize all global products through singular-value shrinkage, and study strict-saddle geometry by viewing W and H as a regularized matrix factorization.
method.mechanism: For fixed bias, the target Y-b1^T is decomposed by SVD and the optimal rank-d product WH soft-thresholds its singular values by sqrt(lambda_W lambda_H). The bias is then optimized analytically, yielding dimension- and regularization-dependent NC regimes. A negative-curvature construction establishes the strict-saddle property for the factorized no-bias problem, while a prior smooth-convex-loss argument is invoked for the biased d>K case. A two-dimensional fixed-ETF slice motivates alpha,M rescaling, and single-run ResNet18 experiments probe optimizers, feature dimensions, fixed classifiers, and rescaling.
assumptions: Every class has exactly n training samples and one-hot labels are uniformly weighted.
Each last-layer training feature is an independent free variable rather than the output of shared network parameters.
The classifier, features, and bias receive separate positive quadratic penalties.
The vanilla-MSE theorem is interpreted only for the stated lambda_W lambda_H, lambda_b, and d regimes.
The full biased strict-saddle theorem assumes d>K so W has a nontrivial null space.
Optimization consequences rely on algorithms and conditions that avoid strict saddles and actually converge.
The rescaled-loss visualization fixes W to a simplex ETF, fixes b=0, varies one feature in a two-vector plane, and uses a large-K limit for its vector-field argument.
End-to-end ResNet behavior is treated as evidence for the free-feature surrogate despite parameter sharing and different regularization.
Single seeded trajectories are treated as representative without run-level uncertainty.
NC geometry is treated as informative about training and generalization despite the absence of a generalization theorem.

techniques.role: Treats every last-layer training feature as a free optimization variable.
Expresses the optimal regularized low-rank prediction matrix by singular-value soft thresholding.
Optimizes the symmetric bias through its effect on the target singular spectrum.
Separates d<K-1, d=K-1, d=K, and d>K global geometries.
Constructs negative-curvature directions at nonglobal critical factor pairs.
Restricts one feature to a two-dimensional plane around a fixed simplex-ETF classifier.
Weights the correct-class residual by alpha and scales the one-hot target by M.
Tracks within-class variability, classifier ETF error, and self-duality.
Attempts to summarize per-example angular classification margins.
Attempts to estimate the effective dimensionality of within-class features.
Replaces the learned final classifier with a fixed simplex ETF.
Checks every official repository commit, implementation formulas, commands, and result lineage against the paper.

evaluations.setting: ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 without augmentation for 200 epochs using SGD, Adam, or stochastic mini-batch L-BFGS.
evaluations.metric: NC1, NC2, NC3, train/test accuracy, and sorted cosine-margin trajectories.
evaluations.result: All methods reduce collapse metrics, but visible NC2 plateaus remain and test accuracy differs; settings are unmatched and L-BFGS learning rate conflicts with the artifact.
evaluations.baseline: Three optimization algorithms under nominally the same vanilla-MSE task.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-10 ResNet18 dimension sweep spanning d<K-1 and d>=K-1 with augmentation and SGD.
evaluations.metric: NC1, cosine-margin distribution, training accuracy, and test accuracy for MSE; test accuracy for CE.
evaluations.result: Larger d is associated with better MSE fitting and testing, while CE appears less sensitive, but the implementation also changes final-block width and parameter count.
evaluations.baseline: Different feature dimensions and CE versus MSE.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-10 ResNet18 with a learned classifier versus a fixed simplex-ETF final classifier.
evaluations.metric: NC1, NC3, train/test accuracy, and cosine-margin distribution.
evaluations.result: The displayed single runs are broadly comparable, but no uncertainty or direct memory measurement supports a strong efficiency claim.

evaluations.setting: miniImageNet ResNet18 alpha sweep at fixed M under rescaled MSE.
evaluations.metric: NC1, NC3, cosine margin, stated numerical rank, train accuracy, and test accuracy.
evaluations.result: The plots report a positive association with alpha, but the scheduler provenance conflicts and the rank panels are not reproducible from current official code.
evaluations.baseline: Lower alpha values under the same nominal M.

evaluations.setting: miniImageNet ResNet18 M sweep at fixed alpha under rescaled MSE.
evaluations.metric: The same six training and testing measures as the alpha sweep.
evaluations.result: The plots report improved collapse and accuracy with M, without repetitions or a control separating target scale from angular conditioning.
evaluations.baseline: Lower M values under the same nominal alpha.

evaluations.setting: Analytic two-dimensional feature slice with W fixed to a K-simplex ETF and b=0.
evaluations.metric: Loss contours and gradient-vector directions for vanilla MSE, CE, alpha=5 rescaled MSE, and M=5 rescaled MSE.
evaluations.result: Larger alpha or M produces a larger angular component in the chosen slice, but the derivation has an Eq.30 target typo and does not model coupled network optimization.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-10 ResNet18 with d=3 and SGD.
evaluations.metric: Visual scatter of 100 selected training features per class.
evaluations.result: The authors describe CE features as more diverse and discriminative than MSE features, but provide no quantitative or repeated comparison.

evaluations.setting: Static official-code parameter-count reconstruction for learned and fixed classifiers at d=512 and d=10.
evaluations.metric: Trainable parameter count by architecture configuration.
evaluations.result: Fixing the d=512 classifier alone saves about 0.046%; the roughly 20.7% reduction comes from shrinking the final residual block to d=10.

limitations: Global-minimizer theory assumes exactly balanced classes and fixed one-hot regression targets.
The free-feature model removes parameter sharing, nonlinear representation constraints, and end-to-end parameter geometry.
A direct penalty on H is substituted for parameter weight decay using only an analogy and upper-bound argument.
Canonical NC2 fails for d<K-1, and all nondegenerate collapse fails in the large-regularization zero regime.
The full biased strict-saddle theorem is limited to d>K and its proof is delegated to prior work.
The global theory covers vanilla MSE, not the jointly rescaled alpha,M objective used for the large-class experiment.
Strict-saddle geometry is not a convergence theorem for arbitrary optimization methods or practical networks.
The landscape visualization freezes W and b, restricts one h to two dimensions, and takes a K-to-infinity limit.
Equation 30 is inconsistent with Equation 4, Equation 31, and the released implementation.
All neural-network results appear to be single seeded runs without uncertainty estimates.
The optimizer comparison changes batch size, effective method, and possibly learning rate.
The feature-dimension sweep also changes architecture width and capacity.
The fixed-ETF efficiency claim is not supported by measured memory or runtime.
The implemented numerical-rank formula differs from the paper and its result list is never populated.
The implemented cosine-margin numerator differs from the centered paper definition.
Validation on stochastic training augmentations adds an undisclosed source of metric variation.
The miniImageNet scheduler in commands differs from the appendix and the named code path crashes.
The external miniImageNet pickle is unversioned and its layout assumptions are undocumented.
The artifact has no exact executed commit, locked environment, tests, CI, raw results, checkpoints, or figure-generation lineage.
No theorem connects neural collapse to generalization, robustness, calibration, or transfer.
failure_modes: Calling every global optimum an NC solution while ignoring the zero and low-rank regimes.
Using 'best rank-d simplex approximation' as if it uniquely determined a class geometry.
Extending a free-feature strict-saddle theorem to end-to-end SGD without matching assumptions.
Treating the absence of spurious local minima as a universal convergence-rate guarantee.
Using a fixed-optimal-classifier two-dimensional slice to explain coupled high-dimensional training dynamics.
Deriving a landscape from an incorrect incorrect-class target formula.
Reading visibly nonzero NC2 plateaus as convergence to zero.
Attributing unmatched optimizer outcomes solely to optimizer identity.
Changing network width in a purported feature-dimension intervention.
Attributing parameter savings from a narrower backbone to a fixed classifier.
Publishing a metric whose code computes a different formula or never stores the values.
Computing centered cosine denominators with uncentered numerators.
Evaluating each checkpoint on fresh random augmentations when fixed-feature geometry is the target.
Inferring monotone hyperparameter effects from one run with no uncertainty.
Depending on an external unchecksummed dataset pickle and stale README commands.
Assuming the current post-paper repository reproduces historical plots without result artifacts or a tagged snapshot.
Using neural-collapse measures as sufficient evidence of generalization quality.
reusable_insights: State neural-collapse theorems by regime: nonzero threshold, representational dimension, bias penalty, balance, and the precise subset of NC1-NC4 actually proved.
When an eigenspace has repeated singular values, report the entire optimizer equivalence class rather than a nominal best-rank projection.
Separate free-feature landscape claims from end-to-end parameter-landscape claims in both theorem names and experimental conclusions.
A strict-saddle theorem should be paired with an explicit algorithm, step-size/noise conditions, boundedness argument, and convergence target.
For rescaled losses, derive the target vector once and unit-test every closed-form reduction against direct evaluation.
Validate two-dimensional landscape intuitions by measuring full-model Hessian spectra, gradient alignment, and convergence rates while W,H,b co-evolve.
Use matched batch size, function evaluations, line searches, schedules, and hyperparameter tuning when comparing optimizers.
Change representation dimension through a controlled bottleneck that leaves the rest of the backbone and parameter budget fixed.
Decompose efficiency gains into classifier parameters, backbone parameters, optimizer state, activations, and measured peak memory.
Implement scientific metrics once in a tested module and verify analytic examples, invariances, and saved-output schemas.
Evaluate collapse on deterministic canonical training views and separately report augmentation robustness.
Report multiple paired seeds, raw per-run trajectories, confidence intervals, and exact commands for every visual ordering claim.
Publish the executed commit, lock file, dataset checksum, raw metric tables, checkpoints, and figure scripts before claiming reproducibility.
Treat collapse geometry and generalization as separate outcomes unless a theorem or causal intervention links them.
Compare balanced UFM predictions with imbalanced, normalized, deep, nonlinear, and data-aware models before claiming prevalence.
open_questions: Can the biased strict-saddle result be proved directly for d<=K, including all singular-value multiplicities and boundary regimes?
What landscape replaces the simplex description when d<K-1, and which optimizer or initialization selects among its continuum of global subspaces?
Does joint alpha,M rescaling admit a complete global-minimizer and strict-saddle characterization?
Which end-to-end architectures actually realize the free-feature optimum under parameter weight decay?
Can one bound the gap between feature-norm regularization and implicit regularization induced by deep parameter norms?
Do full-model gradient-alignment or Hessian measurements validate the fixed-ETF two-dimensional rescaling intuition?
After matching batches, schedules, tuning budget, and compute, do SGD, Adam, and L-BFGS still approach different NC geometries?
Does the d=K-1 threshold persist when d is changed by a fixed-capacity bottleneck rather than by narrowing a residual block?
How much memory and runtime does a fixed ETF save independently of backbone-width changes?
What are the corrected numerical-rank and cosine-margin curves under deterministic evaluation and multiple seeds?
Can the original Figure 6 raw outputs be recovered, given that current official code never saves numerical rank?
Which scheduler and L-BFGS learning rate produced the published miniImageNet and CIFAR-10 figures?
How do class imbalance, label noise, long tails, and non-one-hot targets alter the MSE optimum?
Does NC under MSE predict calibration, robustness, transfer, or test accuracy after controlling train loss and margin?
How do normalized-feature, deep-UFM, mean-field, and realistic-data theories modify the paper's dimensional and regularization phase diagram?
Can a clean tagged artifact regenerate every panel from raw data with current libraries?

competitive_landscape.title: Prevalence of Neural Collapse during the terminal phase of deep learning training
competitive_landscape.difference: It introduces the NC1-NC4 phenomena across practical classifiers; the target studies a regularized MSE surrogate landscape rather than discovering collapse.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural collapse with unconstrained features
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies MSE collapse dynamics under unconstrained features and motivates the same surrogate; the target adds regularized global regimes and strict-saddle analysis.

competitive_landscape.title: Exploring Deep Neural Networks via Layer-Peeled Model: Minority Collapse in Imbalanced Training
competitive_landscape.difference: It shows how class imbalance changes collapse and can erase minority distinctions, exposing the balanced-data boundary absent from the target's phase diagram.

competitive_landscape.title: A Geometric Analysis of Neural Collapse with Unconstrained Features
competitive_landscape.relationship: Geometric UFM predecessor from the same research line.
competitive_landscape.difference: It characterizes simplex geometry and supports fixed simplex classifiers for CE-style objectives; the target specializes to MSE regularization and dimension/bias regimes.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Collapse Under MSE Loss: Proximity to and Dynamics on the Central Path
competitive_landscape.difference: It analyzes MSE collapse and gradient-flow dynamics on or near a central path; the target instead characterizes global minimizers and factorized strict saddles, but does not give comparable practical discrete-time dynamics.

competitive_landscape.title: An Unconstrained Layer-Peeled Perspective on Neural Collapse
competitive_landscape.relationship: Concurrent global-minimizer competitor cited by the target.
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies MSE global optimality for two- and three-layer unconstrained models, including special bias cases; the target's narrower advance is the more general bias setting and strict-saddle claim.

competitive_landscape.title: Extended Unconstrained Features Model for Exploring Deep Neural Collapse
competitive_landscape.difference: It adds multiple free representation layers and studies progressive collapse, while the target analyzes only the final free feature matrix and affine classifier.

competitive_landscape.title: Limitations of Neural Collapse for Understanding Generalization in Deep Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: It demonstrates that collapse statistics alone do not explain generalization, directly narrowing the target's interpretations of optimizer, dimension, and rescaling test accuracy.

competitive_landscape.title: Imbalance Trouble: Revisiting Neural-Collapse Geometry
competitive_landscape.difference: It revisits simplex geometry when classes are imbalanced, a practical regime excluded by the target's equal-n target spectrum.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Collapse with Normalized Features: A Geometric Analysis over the Riemannian Manifold
competitive_landscape.difference: It analyzes explicit feature normalization on a manifold, replacing the target's quadratic free-feature penalty and changing both scale degeneracy and landscape geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: Are All Losses Created Equal: A Neural Collapse Perspective
competitive_landscape.difference: It systematically compares how objectives influence collapse rather than inferring loss quality from one fixed-ETF slice; it is directly relevant to the target's rescaling motivation.

competitive_landscape.title: Perturbation Analysis of Neural Collapse
competitive_landscape.difference: It quantifies deviations from ideal collapse under perturbations, whereas the target's exact balanced UFM does not bound how real networks depart from its optimum.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Collapse in Deep Linear Networks: From Balanced to Imbalanced Data
competitive_landscape.difference: It retains parameter sharing through a deep linear network and extends from balanced to imbalanced data, addressing two abstractions removed by the target's free H.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Neural Collapse Is Provably Optimal for the Deep Unconstrained Features Model
competitive_landscape.difference: It gives global optimality for hierarchical collapse across multiple free layers; the target's result is shallower but more explicit about MSE bias and feature dimension.

competitive_landscape.title: Generalized Neural Collapse for a Large Number of Classes
competitive_landscape.difference: It develops generalized geometries when the number of classes challenges conventional simplex assumptions, refining the regime the target motivates with miniImageNet rescaling.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Collapse for Cross-entropy Class-Imbalanced Learning with Unconstrained ReLU Feature Model
competitive_landscape.difference: It combines class imbalance with a ReLU-constrained feature model, showing how both data frequencies and nonnegativity alter the free-feature geometry absent from the target.

competitive_landscape.title: Supervised Contrastive Representation Learning: Landscape Analysis with Unconstrained Features
competitive_landscape.difference: It applies landscape analysis to supervised contrastive representation learning, broadening the optimization comparison beyond the target's MSE-versus-CE contour slice.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Collapse versus Low-rank Bias: Is Deep Neural Collapse Really Optimal?
competitive_landscape.difference: It questions whether deep collapse is always optimal when low-rank implicit bias intervenes, sharpening the target's nonunique d<K-1 regime and its architecture extrapolation.

competitive_landscape.title: Beyond Unconstrained Features: Neural Collapse for Shallow Neural Networks with General Data
competitive_landscape.difference: It analyzes actual shallow network parameterization and general data rather than independently optimized training features, directly addressing the target's largest abstraction gap.

competitive_landscape.title: Wide Neural Networks Trained with Weight Decay Provably Exhibit Neural Collapse
competitive_landscape.difference: It proves collapse under actual network parameter weight decay in a wide regime, replacing the target's asserted analogy between parameter norms and a direct H penalty.

competitive_landscape.title: The Persistence of Neural Collapse Despite Low-Rank Bias
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies when collapse survives implicit low-rank structure rather than assuming arbitrary free features, helping distinguish representational selection from the target's degenerate best-rank optimizer set.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Collapse Beyond the Unconstrained Features Model: Landscape, Dynamics, and Generalization in the Mean-Field Regime
competitive_landscape.difference: It analyzes landscape, dynamics, and generalization in a mean-field neural model, supplying the end-to-end and population-level links that the target's training-feature factorization cannot establish.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Collapse is Globally Optimal in Deep Regularized ResNets and Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies global optimality in deep regularized ResNets and Transformers, moving from the target's free H toward the architectures on which its claims were experimentally framed.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Collapse in Cumulative Link Models for Ordinal Regression: An Analysis with Unconstrained Feature Model
competitive_landscape.difference: It replaces nominal one-hot classes with ordered cumulative-link structure, showing how target semantics change collapse geometry beyond the target's MSE one-hot setup.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Neural Regression Collapse
competitive_landscape.difference: It develops collapse phenomena for regression rather than one-hot classification, delimiting which parts of MSE collapse arise from the target geometry versus squared loss itself.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims the first global landscape analysis for vanilla nonconvex MSE under unconstrained features, with only neural-collapse global minimizers, all other critical points strict saddles, a geometric justification for rescaled MSE, and practical verification across optimizers and architectures.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Its strongest evidence is the singular-value characterization of regularized vanilla-MSE optima across feature-dimension and bias regimes and the self-contained strict-saddle construction for the regularized factorization subproblem. It supplements these with a constrained loss slice and single-run CIFAR-10/miniImageNet plots.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is a detailed vanilla-MSE regularization/dimension/bias phase diagram plus an all-d strict-saddle result for the fixed-bias/no-bias factorization. The categorical 'only NC' claim is contradicted by the zero and d<K-1 regimes; the full biased theorem is d>K and imported from prior CE work; MSE NC, UFM, central-path dynamics, and a concurrent global-minimizer analysis were prior art. The rescaled-loss and end-to-end claims remain heuristic, and the official artifact contains metric, scheduler, formula, provenance, and reproduction defects that materially weaken the experiments.
